mcqs.q: The two cell populations of the oral epithelium are:
mcqs.explain: Both keratinized and non-keratinized oral epithelium contain keratinocytes (the majority) and non-keratinocytes.

mcqs.q: The four layers of keratinized oral epithelium, from deep to superficial, are:
mcqs.explain: Keratinized epithelium has four layers: stratum basale, spinosum, granulosum and corneum (deep → superficial).

mcqs.q: The basal layer (stratum basale) is also known as the stratum germinativum because it:
opts: Synthesizes DNA and undergoes mitosis, providing new cells
mcqs.explain: The basal layer synthesizes DNA and undergoes mitosis to provide new cells, hence 'stratum germinativum'.

mcqs.q: Cells of the stratum spinosum appear joined by:
mcqs.explain: Spinous cells are larger, irregularly polyhedral, and on light microscopy appear connected by 'intercellular bridges' (desmosomes); they contain membrane-coating granules (glycolipids).

mcqs.q: The non-keratinized oral epithelium has three layers:
mcqs.explain: Non-keratinized epithelium consists of the stratum basale, stratum intermedium and stratum superficiale.

mcqs.q: Orthokeratinized epithelium differs from parakeratinized in that its surface cells:
mcqs.explain: In orthokeratinized epithelium the surface cells lose their nuclei (true keratin); in parakeratinized epithelium they retain shrunken pyknotic nuclei.

mcqs.q: The process by which a keratinocyte migrates and undergoes biochemical/morphologic change is called:
mcqs.explain: Differentiation is the biochemical and morphologic change a keratinocyte undergoes as it migrates upward, ending in a keratinized squama.

mcqs.q: The shedding of surface epithelial cells is termed:
mcqs.explain: Desquamation is the shedding/casting off of cells at the surface; maturation is the migration from basal layer to surface.

mcqs.q: The turnover time of oral epithelium compared with skin, and non-keratinized vs keratinized, is:
opts: Oral faster than skin; non-keratinized faster than keratinized
Oral slower than skin; keratinized faster
Oral mucosa does not turn over
mcqs.explain: Oral mucosa turns over faster than skin, and non-keratinized oral epithelium turns over faster than keratinized.

mcqs.q: The end product of keratinocyte differentiation is:
opts: A keratinized squama — a dead cell of densely packed protein in a toughened membrane
mcqs.explain: Differentiation ends with a keratinized squama: a dead, flattened cell filled with densely packed protein within a toughened cell membrane.

mcqs.q: The basement membrane stains positively with which method (due to its mucopolysaccharides)?
mcqs.explain: The basement membrane contains neutral mucopolysaccharides (GAGs) and stains positively with the periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) method.

mcqs.q: Ultrastructurally, the basal lamina consists of a:
opts: Lamina lucida (clear, near epithelium) and lamina densa (dark, near connective tissue)
mcqs.explain: The basal lamina has a lamina lucida (clear zone below the epithelium) and a lamina densa (dark zone adjacent to the connective tissue).

mcqs.q: The basement membrane contains the protein laminin and:
mcqs.explain: The basement membrane contains laminin and type IV collagen.

mcqs.q: Desmosomes use which transmembrane glycoprotein?
mcqs.explain: Desmosomes use cadherins (desmoglein and desmocollin) and attach epithelial cells in the spinosum, basale and granulosum layers.

mcqs.q: Hemidesmosomes attach basal epithelial cells to the basement membrane using:
mcqs.explain: Hemidesmosomes use integrins to anchor the basal cells of the epithelium to the underlying basement membrane.

mcqs.q: Which non-keratinocyte produces melanin pigment?
mcqs.explain: Melanocytes produce melanin pigment within the epithelium.

mcqs.q: The non-keratinocyte that functions as an antigen-presenting (immune) cell is the:
mcqs.explain: Langerhans cells are dendritic antigen-presenting cells involved in the immune response.

mcqs.q: The non-keratinocyte associated with touch sensation (in the basal layer) is the:
mcqs.explain: Merkel cells are sensory (touch) cells located in the basal layer; unlike other non-keratinocytes they have desmosomes.

mcqs.q: Mitotic division of the epithelium occurs in the:
mcqs.explain: Mitosis takes place in the basal cell layer; daughter cells either remain to divide again or migrate upward to differentiate.

mcqs.q: The membrane-coating granules found in the spinous/granular cells are:
mcqs.explain: Membrane-coating granules (lamellar granules) of the spinous and granular layers contain glycolipids and contribute to the permeability barrier.

mcqs.q: The stratum granulosum on H&E staining is:
mcqs.explain: The granular layer is acidophilic (dark pink with H&E) and appears histologically amorphous.

mcqs.q: The whole sequence — mitosis, migration, differentiation, terminal differentiation, desquamation — constitutes:
mcqs.explain: From the onset of determination through to shedding, this whole renewal process is called keratinization (epithelial turnover).

saqs.q: List the four layers of keratinized oral epithelium.
saqs.a: Stratum basale, stratum spinosum, stratum granulosum, stratum corneum.

saqs.q: List the three layers of non-keratinized oral epithelium.

saqs.a: Ortho: surface cells lose their nuclei (true keratin). Para: surface cells retain shrunken (pyknotic) nuclei.

saqs.q: Define differentiation, maturation, desquamation and turnover time.
saqs.a: Differentiation = biochemical/morphologic change of the migrating keratinocyte. Maturation = migration basal→surface. Desquamation = surface shedding. Turnover time = time to divide and pass through the epithelium.

saqs.q: Describe the basement membrane (light & electron microscopy).
saqs.a: Light: 1–4 µm, cell-free, PAS-positive. EM: basal lamina = lamina lucida + lamina densa, containing laminin and type IV collagen.
Desmosomes = cadherins, joining cells (spinosum/basale/granulosum). Hemidesmosomes = integrins, anchoring basal cells to the basement membrane.

saqs.q: Name the non-keratinocytes and their functions.
